title: Suppression windows + admin override flow for SLO-triggered auto actions (with audit logging)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Context
Auto-rollback/pause is being wired to SLO burn-rate evaluation. We need a safe, auditable way to suppress auto actions during known incidents / telemetry issues / planned experiments, and an admin-only override path that is time-bound and visible in Console + logs.

Problem
Without suppression/override controls:
- Oncall cannot quickly stop repeated auto actions during a known incident (or during monitor/telemetry degradation), causing churn and noise.
- We risk either disabling the feature broadly (losing protection) or allowing unsafe rollbacks (SLA risk).
- Compliance and incident retros need an explicit audit trail for: who suppressed, why, for what scope, and when it expired.

Goals
1) Suppression windows
- Allow creating a suppression that prevents auto actions (rollback/pause/traffic-shift) for a specific scope.
- Scope must support at minimum: service/route + model + region + customer tier, matching the rollout scope semantics.
- Suppression must be time-bound (TTL) with server-side enforcement.
- Suppression should not disable evaluation/telemetry collection; it should only suppress the action step.

2) Admin override flow
- Add admin-only endpoints to create/clear suppressions (and optionally extend) with required justification.
- Enforce RBAC permission checks (see INT-8832).
- Emit audit events for create/update/delete/expire operations and for action attempts suppressed due to an active suppression.

3) Audit logging
- Follow ADR-0128 audit trail schema requirements: required fields, retention expectations, and privacy constraints.
- Audit must cover both:
  a) administrative changes (who set suppression/override)
  b) controller decisions (auto action suppressed + why)

Non-goals
- Complex policy templates UX in this ticket (Console policy editor work tracked separately).
- Permanent suppressions (must always be time-bound).
- Fully autonomous incident detection (suppression is a manual/admin tool).

Proposed semantics
- Suppression applies to auto actions only. Rollout controller continues to evaluate SLO status and emits metrics, but chooses DECISION=SUPPRESSED instead of executing an action.
- Suppression is evaluated before any action decision is executed (rollback/pause/shift). If suppression is active, we skip execution and record suppression reason.
- Default max TTL: 24h (guardrail). Extension requires admin call + new audit event.
- Suppression precedence:
  - If multiple suppressions match, choose the most specific scope match; in practice we can treat as “any match suppresses actions” and include the selected suppression_id in audit.
- Expiration:
  - Expired suppressions should be treated as inactive; we should not require a background job for correctness. Optional cleanup job for storage hygiene.

API sketch (control plane / policy service)
- POST /v1/rollouts/suppressions
  - body: rollout_id (optional), service, route, model_version (optional), region (optional), customer_tier (optional), action_types (optional; default ALL), ttl_seconds, justification
- PATCH /v1/rollouts/suppressions/{suppression_id}
  - allow extend ttl_seconds (bounded), update justification (append-only preferred; ok to allow set but audit must include old/new)
- DELETE /v1/rollouts/suppressions/{suppression_id}
  - requires justification
- GET /v1/rollouts/suppressions?rollout_id=…&service=… (for Console)

Notes
- Implementation can live in policy/config service (preferred) as it already stores rollout-related policy and has RBAC hooks.
- Rollout controller reads suppression state via existing policy fetch path (avoid adding another dependency in controller).

Audit events
Emit events per ADR-0128 (see links) for:
- suppression.created
- suppression.updated (ttl extension)
- suppression.deleted
- suppression.expired (optional if we have a sweeper; otherwise omit)
- rollout.auto_action_suppressed (controller decision)

Audit fields to include (minimum)
- event_type
- timestamp
- actor_type (user/service)
- actor_id (user id / service name)
- actor_email (if user; if available)
- scope (service, route, model_version, region, customer_tier, rollout_id)
- suppression_id
- ttl_seconds + expires_at
- justification
- policy_version / config_version (if applicable)
- correlation_id / request_id
- evaluated_monitors (ids) + metrics_snapshot_ref (for suppressed controller actions only)

Guardrails
- TTL bounds: min 5m, max 24h (configurable constant; start hardcoded)
- Rate-limit admin endpoints (prevent accidental paging storms due to repeated toggles)
- Require non-empty justification (min length 15 chars) for create/delete/extend
- Ensure suppression evaluation is fail-safe:
  - If suppression lookup fails (policy service unavailable), default to NOT suppressed (continue existing safe behavior) but emit metric/controller log “suppression_lookup_failed”. (We debated fail-closed; SRE prefers fail-open to preserve protection.)

Open questions
- Should suppression optionally apply only to rollback but not pause? Proposal: allow action_types filter (ALL by default). PM/SRE to confirm.
- Should we allow rollout_id-only suppressions? Proposal: yes (most common during incidents), but still include service/route for searchability.

Implementation tasks
- Add suppression model + persistence in policy/config service (or existing rollout policy store).
- RBAC wiring for new endpoints (align with INT-8832 permission name).
- Controller: read suppression state from policy result and short-circuit execution; emit decision outcome + audit event.
- Console API: expose suppression list for rollout detail view (depends on ENG-4831).
- Metrics: increment “rollback_suppressed”/“pause_suppressed” with suppression_reason label (bounded set).

Refs
- Project scope item: “do not rollback during known incident overrides.”
- ADR-0128: rollout audit trail schema for auto actions.
- PR-28511: admin override suppress auto rollback (initial implementation; this ticket formalizes suppression windows + audit requirements).
acceptance_criteria:
- Can create a time-bound suppression for a rollout scope and verify controller does not execute auto actions while suppression is active.
- Suppression requires admin permission and non-empty justification.
- Suppression TTL is enforced with safe bounds (min + max), and extend/delete operations are audited.
- Controller emits an audit event for “auto action suppressed” including suppression_id and decision context.
- Console can fetch suppressions for a rollout (at minimum via API; UI polish tracked elsewhere).
- Unit + integration tests cover: matching logic, TTL expiration behavior, RBAC denial, and audit emission.
- Runbook link or short operational note added describing how oncall uses suppression (full runbook tracked in ENG-4855).
implementation_notes:
Current approach (recommended)
- Store suppressions in policy/config service next to rollout policy config to keep a single source of truth.
- Policy evaluation response to controller includes:
  - suppression_active (bool)
  - suppression_id
  - suppression_expires_at
  - suppression_action_types (optional)
  - suppression_justification (do NOT return full text to non-admin callers; use summary/hashed reference if needed)

Matching
- Exact match on keys provided. Fields omitted in suppression are treated as wildcards.
- If multiple matches, pick the one with:
  1) rollout_id match > no rollout_id
  2) more specified fields (service+route+model+region+tier)
  3) latest created_at (tie-break)

Privacy
- Justification is internal-only; ensure Console exposure respects RBAC. For non-admin viewers, return “suppressed by admin” + expires_at.

Failure modes
- Policy service temporarily stale: controller may not see a newly created suppression for a short window. Mitigation: incident-bot message should recommend also pausing rollout manually if immediate mitigation is required.
- Clock skew: use server timestamps in policy service; controller uses expires_at from server.

Integration points
- Event stream emission should use the same audit sink as rollout auto actions (see PR-28435).
- Permission naming/ownership should match INT-8832; security review required (Kevin Osei).
test_plan:
- Unit tests (policy service)
  - TTL bounds validation
  - matching logic + precedence
  - RBAC enforcement (allowed/denied)
  - audit event payload contains required fields
- Unit tests (controller)
  - suppression_active => decision outcome SUPPRESSED and no executor call
  - suppression_action_types filter works (if implemented)
- Integration test (staging)
  - create suppression during an active canary; inject SLO breach; verify no rollback/pause executed; verify audit log + metrics
  - delete suppression; breach persists; verify action executes per policy
- Regression
  - ensure existing rollouts without suppression behave unchanged
rollout_plan:
- Gate behind feature flag: rollouts.auto_actions.suppression (default off)
- Enable in staging for internal canary services (per ENG-4850)
- Enable in prod for one internal route (low blast radius) + SRE signoff
- Publish oncall note + link in #eng-oncall; ensure incident-bot message includes “suppression available” hint
- Monitor metrics: suppressed decisions count, admin endpoint usage, audit event volume
comments: 2026-02-11 (Rafael Mendes): SRE ask coming out of game day: we need a way to suppress auto rollback during known telemetry lag windows (esp. when Mimir ingest is delayed) and during active incidents where we’re intentionally holding a rollout to gather data. Please make sure this is time-bound + auditable; we don’t want “set and forget” disablement.

2026-02-13 (Jordan Lee): Drafted API + semantics above. Key decision: fail-open if suppression lookup fails (continue protection). If policy service is down and we fail-closed, we could miss a rollback during a real regression. Added metric for lookup failures so we can alert on sustained errors.

2026-02-14 (Benji Okafor): Suggest we model suppressions as a first-class resource in config service (not embedded inside rollout policy blob) so we can list/search independently and avoid frequent policy version bumps. OK either way but listing/search is useful for Console + audits. If we keep it embedded, we need to ensure policy version increments don’t trigger rollout policy reevaluation loops.

2026-02-17 (Felix Schneider): For Console, please return a redacted suppression record for non-admin users (expires_at + scope + created_by role). Full justification text should be admin-only. Also ensure audit timeline can link to suppression_id.

2026-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): SRE preference: suppression should default to ALL action types, but we likely need option to suppress rollback only (keep auto-pause) for noisy error spikes where pausing is safe but rollback may not be desired. If we can’t do action_types in MVP, document limitation and default to ALL.

2026-02-20 (Kevin Osei): Security review notes: (1) justification must be mandatory; (2) actor identity must be captured from auth token, not client-provided; (3) ensure audit payload excludes customer prompt content; (4) add rate-limiting and RBAC checks for list endpoint. Approved direction pending implementation details in PR.

2026-02-24 (Jordan Lee): PR up (WIP) extends PR-28511 to include TTL bounds + audit event fields per ADR-0128. Added controller decision event “rollout.auto_action_suppressed”. Waiting on RBAC permission name from INT-8832 to finalize.

2026-02-26 (Connor O'Brien): For release train: keep feature flag default OFF in prod. We’ll enable per-service via config after SRE signoff and after dashboards/alerts are in place to avoid silent suppressions.
